I'll take Version B. This is the exact thing I flagged earlier — the same page arriving with a bunch of "utm" newsletter-tracking junk stuck on the end. In Version A it counted that as a brand-new page and would've made me a second copy of the Rome guide, which is precisely the clutter I'm trying to avoid. Version B saw through the tracking bits, recognized it as the one I already have, and brought up my existing bookmark to tweak instead. That's what I want.

I'm glad you were careful about how far this goes, though — I wouldn't want it getting overeager and treating every little difference in the address as throwaway. Some of what comes after the "?" genuinely points to a different page (a specific article number, a page-two, that kind of thing), and I'd be upset if it merged two genuinely different pages into one because it assumed the tail didn't matter. So as long as it's only the recognizable tracking tags it strips — the marketing "where did you come from" stuff — and it leaves meaningful address details alone, Version B is the behavior I want.
